plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil, and is widely cultivated for ornamental use, essential oils, and as a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely derives from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves that repel water and striking flowers rising above the surface on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters and begins its peak bloom in early summer.
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and northern Australia; cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been germinated after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the flower's surface is so water-repellent it inspired the term 'lotus effect' in materials science.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy North American prairie perennial with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping pink-purple petals around a spiky orange-brown central cone. It is popular in gardens, tolerates drought, and attracts pollinators and goldfinches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; cultivated globally
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiky central cone, and the plant has been used in traditional Native American medicine.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Not in peak bloom everywhere on July 3, but in the Northern Hemisphere's tropics and in some subtropical areas, scattered late flowering occurs. Better examples of Southern Hemisphere winter bloomers are Protea cynaroides, a bold shrub with huge, bowl-shaped flower heads surrounded by pink bracts, flowering in southern African winter and spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics; some trees flower sporadically afterward
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Los Angeles, Florida, Mediterranean regions, and parts of Asia and Africa
plants.funFact: Jacaranda trees in Pretoria, South Africa, are so numerous that the city is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', and their fallen flowers carpet streets in purple.
